fact.thing: times SOXX fell 25% or more from a high in the 10 years before the 2026 drop
fact.box: iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), price only, dividends not included
fact.claim: Over the last 10 years, before this year's drop, SOXX fell 25% or more from a high four times. The troughs were Dec 24, 2018 (−26.1%), Mar 20, 2020 (−34.3%), Oct 14, 2022 (−46.2%) and Apr 8, 2025 (−41.7%). Each time the price later got back above its old high, between 4 months and 2 years after the trough. At the Nov 4, 2026 close SOXX was 31.2% below its Jun 22, 2026 high and had not recovered, and a past recovery does not promise a future one.

why.line: SOXX is one basket of US chip companies, including the ones powering AI.
why.line2: It holds just 30 stocks, all from one industry.
why.means: Every holding depends on the same chip cycle, so the basket has no other industry to cushion a fall, and that is why it dropped 25% or more four times in ten years; it also means a fall hits the whole sector at once instead of one broken company, which is why past drops have been bought back.
